name: The Medina (Great Mosque quarter)
tagline: Living inside a UNESCO World Heritage old town
description: The whitewashed, blue-doored walled medina around the Great Mosque of Uqba is Kairouan at its most atmospheric. Narrow lanes wind past carpet workshops, makroudh bakeries, and centuries-old monuments, all explored on foot. Staying here means history at your doorstep, though comfort and connectivity are basic.
bestFor: Culture lovers, photographers, slow travelers who want to live inside the heritage
pros: Steps from the Great Mosque and major monuments
Everything walkable within the old walls
cons: Can be noisy and busy near the main sites

name: Aghlabid Basins and Sidi Sahbi area
tagline: Medieval reservoirs and the Barber's Mosque
description: Just north and west of the medina, this area gathers two landmarks: the medieval Aghlabid Basins, vast circular water reservoirs, and the serene Zaouia of Sidi Sahbi, known as the Barber's Mosque, with its beautiful tilework. Quieter than the core, it blends heritage with more open, modern streets.
bestFor: Visitors who want landmarks nearby with a bit more breathing room
pros: Close to the Aghlabid Basins and Sidi Sahbi
Less crowded than the medina core
More open streets and easier movement
cons: Fewer atmospheric lanes than the old town

name: Ville Nouvelle (modern town)
tagline: The practical, everyday side of Kairouan
description: Outside the medina walls, the ville nouvelle is Kairouan's modern town of wider streets, shops, cafes, banks, and everyday services. Less picturesque but more functional, it is where you handle practical life, find a local SIM, and settle into a more conventional apartment stay.
bestFor: Longer stays needing services, shops, and a more practical base
pros: Shops, cafes, banks, and services nearby
cons: Lacks the charm of the old medina

name: Sousse (coastal base)
tagline: A larger seaside city about an hour away
description: For heavier work weeks or beach time, Sousse on the coast, roughly an hour from Kairouan by louage or bus, makes a strong complementary base. This larger city offers better connectivity, a wider range of accommodation, restaurants, nightlife, its own UNESCO medina, and easy transport links.
bestFor: Nomads needing reliable wifi, beaches, and more amenities alongside Kairouan visits
pros: Own UNESCO medina and transport hub
cons: About an hour from Kairouan's heritage
More touristy and pricier than Kairouan
